drivingQuestion: What is Rav's reason for forbidding an eiruv through windows where a gentile lives in the alleyway?
outcomeNote: Because Rav includes a courtyard, his reason is the ban on an individual living among gentiles, confirmed by R' Tavla's saying.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מָבוֹי שֶׁצִּידּוֹ אֶחָד גּוֹי וְצִידּוֹ אֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל — אֵין מְעָרְבִין אוֹתוֹ דֶּרֶךְ חַלּוֹנוֹת לְהַתִּירוֹ דֶּרֶךְ פְּתָחִים לַמָּבוֹי.
segments.en: «Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:» With regard to «an alleyway, one side of which» was occupied by «a gentile and one side of which» was occupied by «a Jew,» and the house of the Jew was connected to the houses of other Jews via windows but not via doors, and those other houses open directly into the public domain, the residents of the houses on the side of the alleyway where the Jews live «may not establish an eiruv through the windows» in order «to render» it «permitted» for the residents of the other houses to carry «through the doors» of the house leading «to the alleyway.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: אָמַר רַב אֲפִילּוּ בְּחָצֵר? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, דְּאִי לָא אָמַר מַאי?
segments.en: «Abaye said to Rav Yosef:» Did «Rav say» this «even with regard to a courtyard,» one side of which was occupied by a gentile and the other side of which was occupied by a Jew whose house was connected through windows to the houses of other Jews? «He said to him: Yes, as» even «if he did not say» so, «what» would be the difference? It is the exact same principle.

segments.he: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא טַעְמָא דְּרַב מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר: אֵין מָבוֹי נִיתָּר בְּלֶחִי וְקוֹרָה עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ בָּתִּים וַחֲצֵירוֹת פְּתוּחִין לְתוֹכוֹ.
segments.en: Abaye responded: «I would have said» that «the rationale for» the opinion of «Rav is because he holds» that «an alleyway cannot be rendered permitted» for carrying within it «with a side post and» a cross «beam unless there are houses and courtyards opening into it.»

segments.he: וְתַרְתֵּי לְמָה לִי! צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי מֵהַהִיא —
segments.en: Rav Yosef said: If that were the reason, «why» would «I need two» rulings regarding the same issue? Rav already stated that an alleyway can be rendered permitted for carrying within it only if it has houses and courtyards opening into it. Abaye explained that both rulings are «necessary. As, if» Rav had taught this halakha only «from that» general ruling,

segments.he: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: דִּירַת גּוֹי שְׁמָהּ דִּירָה, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּדִירַת גּוֹי לֹא שְׁמָהּ דִּירָה. וְאִי מֵהָכָא — הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: לָא יָדַעְנָא בָּתִּים כַּמָּה, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן בָּתִּים תְּרֵין.
segments.en: «I would have said» that «the residence of a gentile is considered a residence» with regard to defining an area as an alleyway. Therefore, he «teaches us that the» legal «status of the residence of a gentile is not considered a» full-fledged «residence» in this regard. «And if» Rav had taught this halakha only «from» the ruling «here,» with regard to gentiles, «I would have said» that «I do not know how many houses there» are. Therefore, he «teaches us» that there must be at least «two houses» and two courtyards.

segments.he: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַב אֲפִילּוּ חָצֵר, טַעְמָא דְּרַב דְּקָא סָבַר אָסוּר לַעֲשׂוֹת יָחִיד בִּמְקוֹם גּוֹי.
segments.en: «Now that Rav» has «said» that this halakha applies «even» to «a courtyard,» this implies that «the reason for» the opinion of «Rav is that he holds: It is prohibited for an individual to establish» his home «in the place» where «a gentile» resides. Consequently, he is prohibited from establishing an eiruv, so that the difficulties of living there will force him to move.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִי הָכִי הַיְינוּ דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי טַבְלָא דְּאָמַר: ״גּוֹי גּוֹי״ תְּרֵי זִימְנֵי, וְלָא יָדַעְנָא מַאי אָמַר.
segments.en: «Rav Yosef said: If so, this is» why «I heard Rabbi Tavla say: A gentile, a gentile, two times» while teaching this subject, even though «I did not understand» then «what he» meant to «say.» Now I realize that he was speaking about both an alleyway and a courtyard.
